Scheduler runs the four scheduled Lambda functions, and the one schedule group holds their schedules (Scheduler cutover).
Each scheduled job gets a schedule that replaces its EventBridge rule. The pruner's exists only when enable_quarantine_pruner is true.
Scheduler assumes one new invocation role per job, and the role replaces the Lambda permission for events.amazonaws.com. The pruner's exists only when enable_quarantine_pruner is true.
Each invocation role has an inline policy that allows lambda:InvokeFunction on its one function. The pruner's exists only when enable_quarantine_pruner is true.
Scheduler replaces the four scheduled EventBridge rules. There is no state move from a rule to a schedule.
The rules' targets go with the rules. Each schedule has its own target.
Scheduler invokes through an execution role, so the events.amazonaws.com permissions on the four functions are no longer needed.
The ownership marker records the create_iam value a stack first applied with, and blocks any later change to it. Every stack gets one.

Every statement in a module-generated trust gets a Sid. The API handler trust also drops lambda.amazonaws.com outside the Lambda API path. Roles that use the shared ECS trust document change too, but the mock returns fixed policy-document JSON, so they show no diff here.
Every statement in the module's managed policies gets a Sid, and existing Sids are renamed to the effect-first pattern. IAM stores a new default policy version.
Every statement in the module's inline policies gets a Sid, and existing Sids are renamed to the effect-first pattern. PutRolePolicy updates each in place.
The nine key-policy Sids are renamed to the effect-first pattern. This is a one-time PutKeyPolicy; the root kms:* statement keeps its permissions under its new Sid.
The customer listener gets the shared tags that its internal-listener sibling already has.
The customer listener's path rules get the shared tags that their internal-listener siblings already have.
